exposure: Subtypes of fetal growth restriction (FGR) (early-onset, late-onset, preeclamptic, recurrent FGR)

Placental histopathology (diffuse maternal/fetal vascular malperfusion, villitis of unknown etiology, decreased percentage of intact terminal villi, villous capillarization ratio, avascular villi, infarction)
outcome: Birth weight below the second percentile
cohort: The study included 61 cases of fetal growth restriction (FGR) classified according to the Amsterdam criteria.
finding: In early-onset-FGR and preeclamptic FGR, altered vascularization of villi may play a key role in pathogenesis, while recurrent FGR is associated with villitis of unknown etiology; additionally, a femoral length/abdominal circumference ratio >0.26 is associated with specific histopathological alterations of the placenta in FGR pregnancies.
birth_weight: Birth weight below the second percentile
